demoScript.title: Ordinary Tuesday
demoScript.caption: Six LA ZIPs, real SCE June-2024 usage. On a normal day the Base Core fleet sells stored energy above each home's protected reserve during the evening peak.

demoScript.title: Second customer: utility DR dispatcher
demoScript.caption: Same fleet, second buyer. A demand-response dispatcher asks for feeder relief: accepted load deferrals first, battery energy above reserve second, the rest handed back.

demoScript.title: Fire-weather warning
demoScript.caption: A fire-weather shutoff warning arrives (scenario; the bundled NWS snapshot is shown for context). Residents get a reviewed Prepare-now alert. Simulated outbox only, nothing is sent.

demoScript.title: Staggered preparation vs 4 PM rush
demoScript.caption: If everyone plugs in at 4 PM, demand spikes past the feeder's spare capacity. PoweruP staggers charging over 18 hours, most at-risk homes first, inside the shared limit.

demoScript.title: Dispatcher approves the budget
demoScript.caption: A human approves the plan. Only loads residents accepted can be reduced; essential loads are never touched. No real commands are sent.

demoScript.title: Outage hours 0–72
demoScript.caption: Power goes out at 6 PM. Each home now has a grace-period budget: how many kW it can draw so essential loads last the full 72 hours.

demoScript.title: 3 AM: connection loss
demoScript.caption: At 3 AM four batteries go quiet. They keep following the local plan they already have. PoweruP sorts them: not talking, breaker tripped, or broken, and stops counting them as verified capacity.

demoScript.title: Handoff to the operator
demoScript.caption: What the fleet cannot cover goes to a human operator, with every decision logged: home shortfalls, silent batteries, and critical loads with no grace period.
